requirement_text.REQ-047: Port src/engine/instance.zig's InstanceStore.applyTransition() (per src/design/engine.md "Section EE-03: Task Activation", L1086) as the persistence orchestration layer that turns REQ-044's pure transition output into committed rows. This is the seam between the I/O-free kernel and the database. Given a transition result whose pending_task_nodes gained an entry, insert a REQ-043 tasks row with status PENDING, task id, instance_id, token_id, node_id, node_name, assignee_type and assignee_ref taken from the HUMAN_TASK node's attributes (REQ-029's PD-05 rules already guarantee a HUMAN_TASK carries a non-empty role). The tasks row insert, the instance_projections state update, and the event append via REQ-025 all commit in ONE transaction (EE-03 AC2, DB-03). A task must never be visible to a reader before the transition that created it is committed (EE-03 AC5). No node-type guard is written in this layer: engine.md section EE-03's module purpose is explicit that the transition function only ever appends HUMAN_TASK nodes to pending_task_nodes, so "the signal itself is the guard." Port that property rather than re-implementing a START/END/gateway exclusion check here -- but assert it with a test (EE-03 AC3/AC4) so the property is verified rather than assumed. A HUMAN_TASK whose assignee_ref names a group with no current members still creates a PENDING task; assignment resolution is deferred to runtime (EE-03 edge case), not an activation-time failure. A token entering an END node transitions the instance to COMPLETED and creates no task. R-Co's EE-03 edge case also fires SCH-03 timer cancellation at that point -- src/scheduler/ is S6 (operational-cross-cutting) and does not exist in Letflow, so port the COMPLETED transition and leave a named, documented hook for timer cancellation rather than silently omitting it or inventing a scheduler. SCOPE BOUNDARY: GET /api/v1/tasks and the task list/query surface are S4 (api-surface) plus R-Co's own src/tasks/store.zig, outside this stage's src/engine/ scope per REQ-043's note. This requirement writes tasks rows from the engine; it does not build the read side.

task.description: Design the persistence orchestration layer for REQ-047 (task activation persistence). You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ047-20260818. Read lib/letflow/design/ for the existing REQ-043 (tasks table/schema), REQ-044 (pure transition kernel, Letflow.Engine.Token / transition function), and REQ-045 (instance start engine shell, including its worklist loop advance_until_stable/4) design docs and shipped code -- REQ-047 is the seam that takes REQ-044's pure transition output and REQ-045's dispatch loop and persists task activation atomically. Also read docs/migration/stage-3-instance-engine.md's EE-03 section and any cited R-Co source (src/design/engine.md around L1086) if present in this repo's migration docs. Write lib/letflow/design/req047-task-activation-persistence.md per WF-02 Step 1's required shape: public function signatures with @spec-style types, key data structures, invariants, DB tables/columns touched, cross-module dependencies, open questions. Cover every acceptance criterion below with a concrete design element -- no TBD/deferred sections, no actual .ex code bodies (signatures/types only).
acceptance_criteria: a transition that enters a HUMAN_TASK node results in exactly one tasks row with status PENDING carrying instance_id, node_id, node_name, assignee_type and assignee_ref, committed in the same transaction as the instance_projections update and the appended event
when the event append fails, zero tasks rows and zero instance_projections changes are committed -- demonstrated by forcing an append failure and reading all three tables back

transitions entering START, END, EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY and PARALLEL_GATEWAY nodes create zero tasks rows, each with its own explicit test, verifying (not merely assuming) the transition function's pending_task_nodes guarantee
a HUMAN_TASK whose assignee_ref names a group with no members still produces a PENDING task rather than an activation error
a token entering an END node sets the instance to COMPLETED, creates no task, and leaves a documented named hook for SCH-03 timer cancellation with S6 identified as its owning stage

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req047-task-activation-persistence.md. Design extends the already-shipped Letflow.Engine.persist/7 Ecto.Multi (REQ-045/050/051, read directly in lib/letflow/engine.ex) with a fifth step, :task_records, via a new Letflow.Engine.TaskActivation module (lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex, not yet created). Key elements: (1) newly_pending_tokens/2 diffs InstanceState.pending_task_nodes before/after one transition/3-driven activation to resolve REQ-044 design doc's own open question (OQ-12.3) on how pending entries are tracked, without ever mutating pending_task_nodes itself; (2) token_id_to_record_id/2 resolves the tasks.token_id FK by zipping new_instance_state.tokens against the already-shipped :token_record Multi step's inserted TokenRecord rows in matching order, since the pure Token.token_id (a caller-minted string, not a UUID for split branches) is never the same value as TokenRecord's DB-autogenerated id -- a real mismatch this design surfaces rather than assumes away; (3) resolve_assignee/1 reads node.attributes['role']/['assignee_type'] with zero group-membership validation, satisfying the group-with-no-members acceptance criterion; (4) cancel_pending_timers/2 is the named, documented SCH-03/S6 hook, called from the existing :finalize step's :completed clause, body specified as unconditional :ok today. Atomicity (same-transaction task/projection/event commit, and zero rows on a forced event-append failure) is achieved with no new transaction mechanism -- append_multi/6 only appends one more Multi.run/3 step to the caller's already-open Multi. Five open questions listed explicitly (OQ-1: assignee_type's source attribute key has no validator pinning it -- PD-05/CHK-09 only guarantees 'role'; OQ-2: node.label-nil fallback to node.id for node_name; OQ-3: form_schema left unset, no source named; OQ-4: the previous-pending-list contract future EE-04 must follow; OQ-5: TaskActivation module naming, no prior precedent). Every acceptance criterion mapped to a concrete design element in section 12's traceability table. No implementation code -- every code block is a @spec, field-mapping table, or algorithm-shape description.
